text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Robert Mugabe has ordered an investigation into the alleged misappropriation of millions of dollars meant for the compensation of war veterans, following revelations that senior government officials were the biggest beneficiaries of the fund.

- A group of Harare businessmen proposed the formation of a new black empowerment pressure group to counter what they call the acquisitive tendencies of Philip Chiyangwa, president of the Affirmation Action Group.

- Telecel International, the company that won the tender to operate a second cellular phone service in Zimbabwe, said on Thursday it was going ahead with plans to implement the project despite a directive by the tender board to suspend the award.
- Telecel says its first priority is to provide cellular service on GSM. Newer technology will only be implemented later to complement that service.

- Commuter trains will start running between the main Harare railway station and several high-density suburbs in Zimbabwe's capital by the end of June if plans by the city council to establish an urban transport authority succeed.
